newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in active trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Monday despite some profit-taking as volume rose to its highest level in more than two years, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.15 percent, or 2.66 points, to 234.92 on all-share turnover of 216 million shekels against 170 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.94 percent higher at 242.92.
"Activity was very high today with total volume at its highest level in more than two years," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"The session opened with a strong rise and by midday the market was up 2.5 percent. Towards the end of the trading day investors started taking profits and the market closed with only a moderate rise," she said.

"The positive momentum continues as institutional investors become more active in the stock market. In the short run we might see some profit-taking but the outlook for the bourse is very positive," said Ronen Kaufman at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"Investors believe that the Bank of Israel will have to reduce its key interest rate following the recent rise of the shekel against the dollar," Kaufman added.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 1.75 percent to 31,390 agorot on volume of 15.4 million shekels; Israel Chemicals, which climbed 2.0 percent to 327 agorot on turnover of 10 million shekels, and Clal Electronics Industries, which ended 3.75 percent higher at 37,622 on volume of 8 million shekels.
